messages:
anna: Heads-up — tenant `org-187` just saturated a few GPU pools. Other tenants on the same node saw 3x tail p99s in the last 2m. Noisy‑neighbor mitigation didn't engage because router picked a cheaper model variant.
raj: Can you paste the spike metrics?
anna: Quick snapshot: tenant_in_flight: 420 -> 1200, per_node_util: 0.44 -> 0.98, route_model_switches: yes, backend_queue_ms p95 went 200->1200.
kevin: Sounds like burst allowed through at gateway level. We're currently only enforcing hard per-key qps at the edge, not gradual smoothing.
lia: We should correlate kv_cache_hit_ratio too — if their cache is cold due to many diverse prompts, it'll multiply GPU work.
michael: From a UX/console POV we want a clear reason for throttles. Users hate opaque 429s. Could we surface "soft throttle" events in the dashboard with suggested remediation? :thinking_face:
anna: Proposal: introduce an internal "soft_throttle" that reduces acceptance probability per-org rather than hard failing, with visible telemetry and a rollout flag.
raj: Implementation debate: do soft throttles live in the API gateway (fast, edge) or in the routing service (having more signals like node queues)? Edge gives fastest enforcement but lacks cache/node signals. Router has context but adds latency to decision.
kevin: My vote: decision at gateway but seeded by a periodic signal from routing/telemetry service. Gateway keeps a per-org smoothing token-bucket that gets an input multiplier from router.
lia: That multiplier should be a compact signal: {burst_score, node_pressure, cache_miss_rate}. Router emits every 5s.
anna: Example config we sketched: 
```
soft_throttle:
  window_seconds: 60
  max_drop_prob: 0.5
  decay_half_life_sec: 30
  route_signal_ttl: 8
  enforcement_mode: "probabilistic"
```
raj: Nice. Also need a detection heuristic for "noisy neighbor" that avoids false positives: require sustained high burst_score for 2 windows or spike + low cache_hit.
kevin: Telemetry names to add to dashboards: tenant_burst_score, tenant_in_flight, per_node_queue_ms_p95, tenant_cache_miss_rate. Set alerts when burst_score>0.8 for 120s.
michael: How will rollouts work? Product wants a canary followed by percentage rollout and an easy disable.
anna: Plan: feature flag "soft_throttle_v2" gated per-org via console. Start 10% random orgs, monitor error budget and latency delta, then 50/100. Rollback if global p99 latency worsens >5% or error_rate increase >0.5% over baseline.
quota-bot: deploy-check: featureflag soft_throttle_v2 exists, gateway schema validated, router signal emitter running in staging.
raj: One more API sketch for operators: POST /admin/tenants/:id/soft_throttle -> {"mode":"set","drop_prob":0.2,"reason":"canary"}. Gateway honors manual overrides immediately.
lia: We'll need dedicated dashboard widget for per-tenant history and a table of current soft_throttle states (drop_prob, source, last_update).
kevin: I'll own the detection + router emitter, raj you own gateway integration, anna you run the canary and console UX with michael.
anna: I'll open a short RFC + rollout playbook. TL;DR: probabilistic soft throttles enforced at gateway seeded by router signals, canary via flag, dashboard + alerts included.
michael: Perfect — thanks. I'll add a small console mock to the RFC so PMs can sign off. :+1:
